About the Role
Anthropic's inference fleet serves Claude to millions of users across our own products and the world's largest cloud platforms. The stack that makes this possible is deep and tightly coupled: accelerator kernels, model servers, distributed routing, autoscaling, capacity management. Every layer affects the others, often in ways that are hard to see in isolation.

The Inference System Dynamics team is responsible for understanding that whole system and holding it to a high bar across four dimensions: throughput, latency, reliability, and correctness. We measure how the fleet performs against its theoretical performance frontier, run cross-layer investigations to explain the gaps, and own the correctness checks that make sure Claude's outputs are right, not just fast, across hardware platforms and serving configurations. We don't own the individual components. We instrument and model them, find the highest-leverage opportunities across them, and partner with the owning teams to land the wins.

You'll work across all four areas. One week that might mean tracing a tail-latency regression from request timing down through routing and batching into a kernel overhead; the next it might mean tightening a correctness eval so it catches an output regression introduced by a quantization change. We're looking for performance engineers who treat correctness as part of performance.

Key Responsibilities
Run cross-layer performance investigations across throughput, latency, and reliability, sizing the gap between actual fleet performance and theoretical rooflines, identifying root causes, and quantifying the value of closing them
Own and improve the correctness evaluation pipeline that validates model output quality across hardware platforms, numerics, and serving configurations, and lead the investigation when it catches a regression
Build the observability, dashboards, and modeling tools that make throughput, latency, cost, reliability, correctness, and their interactions legible across the stack
Partner with kernel, serving, routing, autoscaling, and capacity teams to prioritize and land the highest-impact optimizations your analysis surfaces

Job Description:

Robotics Quality Engineer

Location: Fremont, CA - Onsite

We are seeking a Product Quality & Reliability Engineer, in Fremont, CA to serve as the technical quality lead for Nextpower's robotic and electronic systems. This role owns product-level quality from design through field performance, ensuring seamless integration of hardware, firmware, and electromechanical subsystems. Partnering cross-functionally with design, manufacturing, and suppliers, this individual will embed quality early in the product lifecycle, lead reliability validation and NPI activities, and drive data-driven improvements across PCBA, motion control, sensor, and embedded systems. The ideal candidate combines strong electronics and mechatronics expertise with hands-on validation experience, supplier quality leadership, and a passion for building robust, high-performing products.

Responsibilities:

 

Product Quality Ownership

Serve as the technical quality lead for robotic and electronic products—ensuring hardware, firmware, and electromechanical integration meet Nextracker standards.

Partner with design, test, and manufacturing engineering to embed quality and reliability controls early in the product lifecycle.

Define, implement, and validate product test and inspection requirements across PCBA, harness, motion control, and sensor subsystems.

Support new product introduction (NPI) through DFMEA/PFMEA execution, control plan creation, and design verification test (DVT) oversight.

Validate and qualify test systems and automated inspection tools for functional verification of complex assemblies.

Drive product-level reliability testing (HALT, HASS, burn-in, and environmental stress screening) and feed results into design improvements.

 

Supplier & Component Quality

Evaluate and approve suppliers for electronic and robotic assemblies—PCBs, actuators, control boards, sensors, and embedded systems.

Audit supplier facilities to confirm process capability, traceability, and quality control for critical components.

Lead technical reviews on defect trends, early-life failure data, and product field returns (RMA/FA), driving corrective and preventive action.

Implement statistical process control (SPC) and advanced data analytics (Cp, Cpk, Weibull, X̄-R) to monitor and improve part and system performance.

Develop, implement, and maintain supplier quality scorecards with metrics that emphasize reliability and system performance consistency.

 

Cross-Functional Leadership 

Collaborate with hardware and software teams to validate design for manufacturability, serviceability, and long-term reliability.

Translate customer and field feedback into actionable product improvement initiatives.

Support failure investigations through structured root cause methodologies (8D, 5-Why, fault tree analysis) and ensure learnings are applied to future designs.

Champion the “design for quality” mindset across the product organization—linking field performance data directly to design and supplier improvements.

  

REQUIREMENTS 

 

Bachelor’s Degree required (prefer degree in Electrical, Electronics, or Robotics Engineering).

Experience: 3–7 years in product-level quality or reliability engineering for robotics, embedded electronics, or smart devices.

Strong working knowledge of PCBA design and testing, motion control systems, sensors, and firmware integration.

Experience in product validation, DVT/PVT processes, and environmental/reliability qualification testing.

Skilled in Minitab or similar SPC tools, with the ability to interpret product data and drive measurable improvements.

Knowledge of ISO 9001, IATF 16949, or ISO 13485, with hands-on experience in supplier or product audits.

Proficient in GD&T, AQL inspection, and problem-solving frameworks such as DMAIC or DFSS.

 

Language:           Fluent in English

Travel:                  Up to 50% domestic travel, international travel may be required

Work Visa:          Authorized to work in United States 

 

INTERPERSONAL SKILLS 

 

·         Analytical and innovative problem-solver with strong technical grounding in electronics and mechatronics.

·         Skilled communicator who can engage effectively with design, manufacturing, and supplier teams.

·         Naturally curious, driven to understand how products fail and how to make them more robust.

·         Comfortable in both lab and field environments, balancing data analysis with hands-on validation.

·         Adaptable, pragmatic, and capable of leading cross-functional efforts under tight deadlines.

·         Committed to quality excellence, product reliability, and continuous improvement.

Build out property-based and deterministic simulation testing across the software stack.
